senses.gloss: m. (πυργίον, πύργος) burgus) little turret, isolated place of residence, often used as a station for travellers (castellum; v. Sm. Ant. s. v. Mansio).
units: <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 7:4">Lev. R. s. 7</cite> <he>הגיע לב׳ וכ׳</he> he arrived at the first station &c.; Pesik. Eth. Korb. p. 61ᵃ Ar. (ed. <he>בורגנין</he>, <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 479:19">Yalk. Lev. 479</cite>, end <he>כור דגן</he>, corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 10:2">Midr. Till. to Ps. X, 1</cite>.—Pl. <cite ref="B00342"><he>בּוּרְגְּנִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="B00342"><he>בּוּרְגְּנִין</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:12:4">Y. Meg. IV, 75ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>הדר בב׳</he> he who takes lodging in &c. (contrad. to <he>פונדקי</he>).—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 5:1:7">Y. Erub. V, 22ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>ע״י מערות וב׳</he> on account of a connected Sabbath line by means of underground walks and of turrets; (Tosef. ib. VI (V), 8 <he>מגדלות</he>).

<cite ref="Eruvin 21a:7">Erub. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>אין ב׳ בבבל</he> the law as to stations in the neighborhood of towns eventually counted as outskirts for measuring Sabbath limits, cannot be applied to Babylon &c. Ib. 55ᵇ <he>והב׳ שבתוכן</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>שבתוכה</he>) and the station houses in the fields (containing provision and lodging rooms).

<cite ref="Mishnah Maasrot 3:7">Maasr. III, 7</cite>, v. <cite ref="A01948"><he>אִלְקָטִית</he></cite>. Mekh. Yith. Baḥod. 1 <he>הרי … את הבּוּרְגְּסִין ואת הבורגמין וכ׳</he> (read <he>ואת הבּוּרְגִּינִין</he>) ye are now forced to keep in repair the large and small stations for those going to the royal vineyards (prob. to be read <he>כרכים</he> fortresses).—

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 37:3">Lev. R. s. 37</cite>; <cite ref="Eruvin 64b:6">Erub. 64ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:9:3">Y. Ab. Zar. I, 40ᵃ</cite> bot. (<cite ref="B00378"><he>בורנין</he></cite>, corr. acc.); <cite ref="Tosefta Pesachim 1:27">Tosef. Pes. I</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Pesachim 2:27">II</cite>), 27 <he>מעיירות</he> (<he>הללו</he>) <he>של ב׳ אני</he> I am one of those station guards.

<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:30">Lam. R. to I, 4</cite> it does not read (the roads are in mourning) <he>מבלי ב׳ מבלי בוליטין</he> (Ar. <he>בליוטין</he>, read <cite ref="B00869"><he>בַּלִּיסְטִין</he></cite>) because they are not guarded with turrets and catapults. [Midr. Till. l. c. <he>הבורגן</he>, v. <cite ref="B00342"><he>בּוּרְגָּנִי</he></cite>.]
